Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the InnoMed Devices Corporation Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; John Ramirez, CFO; Dr. Michael Chen, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. InnoMed Devices demonstrated significant progress this Q4, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I'll highlight seven key aspects of our performance, starting with our overall results and key achievements, then moving through procedure volumes, R&D investments, new product contributions, our capital versus consumables mix, adoption trends, and our strategic priorities ahead.

Let's begin with our overall performance highlights and key achievements. We're thrilled with how 2023 unfolded as another transformative year for InnoMed, advancing precision medicine through innovative medical devices. On the top line, we delivered full-year revenue of $4.82 billion, up 18% reported and 21% organic on a constant currency basis—beating our initial guidance and marking our best annual showing since the 2019 IPO. Robust procedure volumes across core franchises powered this, with global medtech procedures up 12-14% industry-wide based on our tracking and Leerink Partners data. Adjusting for 300 basis points of FX headwinds, mainly from a strong USD in Europe, organic growth shone even brighter.

By segment, Structural Heart, our biggest at 42% of revenue, surged 28% organically to $2.03 billion, led by 32% TAVR volume growth. Our next-gen EvoFlow TAVR platform, with full FDA approval in Q2 and CE Mark expansion in Q3, grabbed 15% U.S. market share in six months, taking from Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 and Medtronic's CoreValve Evolut. ASPs stayed solid at $32,000 per unit, aided by CMS APC reimbursement updates.

Robotics and Navigation skyrocketed 45% organically to $1.12 billion, now 23% of revenue, riding the minimally invasive surgery wave. The InnoBot Xi system, competing with Intuitive Surgical's Ion, grew its global installed base to 1,250 units—a 55% jump—with consumables up 62% from utilization averaging 22 procedures per system monthly. Our November Siemens Healthineers partnership integrates AI imaging into InnoBot, eyeing deeper inroads in prostatectomies and lung biopsies.

Orthopedics and Extremities grew 14% organically to $985 million, with the Trinity Cementless Hip System gaining amid a 16% U.S. hip replacement rebound post-COVID. We beat Stryker's Mako in select ASCs, where NaviGuide cut OR time 22% per post-market studies.

Diagnostics and Wearables rose 12% to $685 million, powered by CardioLink implantable monitor—rivaling Medtronic's Reveal XT but with 96% AI arrhythmia sensitivity. Emerging markets drove 25% of that growth.

U.S. led at 65% of revenue, up 22% organically, thanks to Inflation Reduction Act pricing stability and expanded Medicare TAVR for low-risk patients. EMEA grew 16% organically despite FX, with Germany and UK tenders for EvoFlow at 70%. APAC flew 28% to $785 million—fastest region—via China NMPA for InnoBot Xi unlocking $2.5 billion TAM, and India's cardiac rise from urbanization.

Operationally, our $250 million Costa Rica facility cut lead times 35%, dodging Mexico tariff risks. R&D hit 11.5% of revenue at $554 million, securing eight FDA 510(k)s and three PMAs, including NeuroStim DBS for Parkinson's with closed-loop tech versus Boston Scientific's Vercise. The Q3 $1.2 billion NeuroVance Therapeutics buy added bioresorbable stents, boosting CV IP 40%.

Under our Precision Growth framework, we prioritize high-margin procedure tech for an aging population—IQVIA sees 7-9% medtech demand to 2030. We gained 220 bps global share, topping industry's 10%, with $3.4 billion backlog up 25% for 2024 visibility.

For FY2024, we're guiding $5.45-$5.60 billion revenue, 13-16% organic, adjusted EPS $6.85-$7.05, factoring $150 million NeuroVance synergies and stable FY2024 IPPS.

In short, 2023 showcased market-leading execution and positioning for double-digit growth.

Now, shifting to procedure volume trends and market recovery. The med devices sector's multi-year COVID recovery has us in expansion, with Q4 volumes up 14% YoY globally—strongest since pre-pandemic. Elective procedures, our core, rebounded sharply.

In Cardiovascular, 45% of revenue, volumes jumped 18% YoY from structural heart and peripherals. TAVR cases rose 25% worldwide as backlogs cleared and EvoValve adoption sped up, with 85% utilization in high-volume centers versus 72% last year—AI imaging cut times 20%. Coronary stents grew 12%, Synergy XD gaining 150 bps share over Boston Scientific's Synergy and Abbott's Xience.

Orthopedics and Spine, 30% mix, saw 11% volume rise. U.S. knees/hips at 105% of 2019, Triad Cementless capturing 220 bps in hips via 30% better osseointegration. Spinal fusions up 13%, Quantum Pedicle Screws with robotics boosting complex cases 16%. Outpatient shift: 28% procedures moving to ASCs on payer push.

Neuromodulation up 9%, DBS 15% from NeuroStim Pro's steering; Endoscopy 10% via FlexScope single-use cutting contamination.

U.S., 55% sales, at 108% pre-COVID, up from 92% Q4 2022—staffing at 95%, backlogs 85% cleared, CMS MS-DRG stability. Europe, 25%, 95% of 2019 but +10% YoY; Germany/UK +13% on DRGs/NICE, France/Italy flat via pricing/value contracts +2-3% ASP. APAC ex-China +16%, Japan/India strong; China 20% but lumpy on NMPA, localized manufacturing de-risks for 25% 2024 growth.

Vantage Robotics in 70% ortho-spine lifts precision, cuts revisions 15%; SurgiLink connects 2,500 ORs, +12% throughput. R&D eyes bioresorbables for PAD.

Volumes outpaced units 300 bps, share to 2.2%, pricing +2% global/U.S. +3%. Tailwinds: aging 65+ +5% YoY, value-based care. Q1 guide +12-15%, supports 11-13% FY organic, 150-200 bps margins.

Next, our R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress. This is central to growth in the $500 billion med devices market, targeting structural heart, neuromodulation, robotics against Medtronic, Boston Scientific, Edwards.

Q4 R&D was $162 million, 11.8% revenue—up from 10.9% prior, YTD $478 million toward $650-675 million FY2024, 14th straight double-digit YoY quarter. Tops Abbott/Stryker at 11-12% target amid easing inflation/supply.

28 programs, 65% U.S./EU on value-based tailwinds. Structural Heart: InnoValve Ultra 12-month IDE data—98% success, 1.2% mortality, <2% leak; PMA Q1 2025, launch H2 U.S./EU MDR mid-year, $1.2 billion peak 40% margins. InnoClip Bio Breakthrough Designation, 95% resorption preclinical; trial topline Q4 2024.

Neuromodulation: AccuStim DBS Phase II 72% responders, +15% UPDRS vs. Medtronic; EU Q4 2024, U.S. IDE Q2 2025, APAC/Japan fast-track. Robotics: InnoBot Precision first-human sub-1mm accuracy, $50 million EU funding, IDE 2025, $20 billion TAM +18% volumes.

AI/digital: CardioSense Pro 96% AFib sensitivity, UK NHS/CE/FDA Q1 2025, China NMPA; 3D-printed PCLA ortho 30% faster integration vs. Zimmer.

Tuck-ins: $120 million bioresorbables, $85 million AI, +15 programs. 1,200 R&D staff +22% YoY, $45 million labs Boston/Galway.

U.S. 60% focus, FDA Q-Sub/IRA; Europe 90% MDR compliant; APAC China +$28 million Q4, Singapore hub for 25% rev 2027.

Expect 18-22% organic to 2027, new products 35% incremental, 4-6x ROI, $8 billion NPV pipeline. R&D 11-13% long-term, FCF >90%.

Moving on to new product launches and their growth contribution. These drove much of our momentum, targeting cardio, diabetes, robotics amid aging/chronic shifts.

InnoGluc Pro CGM, FDA/CE cleared late 2023, AI predicts hypo 30 min/92% accuracy > Dexcom G7/Abbott Libre. Q4 $185 million, 22% Diabetes rev, 15 pts of 32% growth; ASP $450 +5%, Medicare/Japan/UK strong—INNOGLUC-2 +25% time-in-range.

VascuShield TAVR, U.S. March launch post-IDE, 98.5% success/1.2% mortality vs. Sapien/Evolut; $120 million Q4, 28% Structural Heart growth, 10 pts total; FY $500 million ASP $32k, EU/China ramp.

RoboFlex endoscopy De Novo Q1, haptic/7DOF -22% times; $75 million, 45% Endoscopy; ASP $8.5k disposable/$1.2m capital.

Total $380 million/32% Q4 rev, 70% organic ex-FX. R&D $280 million/22% rev +15% YoY.

Ahead of 5.5% med CAGR to $800 billion 2030; targets 12-18% subs. NeuroLink AI $450 million accelerated; five more FY25. New products 25-28% FY24 growth, mid-teens organic.

Now, capital equipment versus consumables mix trends. This highlights our resilient annuity model—capitals like PrecisionNav robotics/CardioGuide imaging, consumables FlexiCath/OrthoLock/NeuroWire disposables.

Q4 mix 28% capital/72% consumables, +200 bps YoY toward 75% FY2026. Consumables +14% organic $1.42 billion on 12% volumes/+2% ASP; capital flat $560 million, disciplined deployments +5% service.

Procedures +12% > iData 8-10%; robotics base +11% to 4,200, 85% util +300 bps, consumables +22% >95% attach like da Vinci multi-specialty.

AI PrecisionNav 2.0 +15% pull-through, +18% cases/2.8 kits; FlexiCath 18% TAVR share +16% consumables.

U.S. 52% rev, 76% consumables +4 pts, ASCs +25% to 1,200 +30% util; capital $280 million backlog $2.1 billion bundled.

EMEA consumables +18% €420 million 70% mix, ortho +15%; capital -4%. APAC 20% $310 million 68%, China/India/Japan.

Prioritize base expansion 12-15%, value contracts 90%+ attach. Pipeline bioresorbables/AR neuro, 6-7% $450 billion CAGR, +3-4% ASP vs. 2% inflation.

Q1 consumables 13-15%, mix 73%, capital mid-single; 80%+ recurring '26, consumables 78% GM vs. 62% capital.

Turning to hospital and ASC adoption rates, key for recurring streams—% target facilities (100+ qual procs/yr) with PrecisionNav/OrthoFlex. Correlates 2.5x util lift, -15-20% revisions PROSPECT data.

Q4 overall 48% core hospitals +450 bps seq/+8% YoY, 127 wins incl. Mayo/Cleveland standardizing joints/spine.

ASCs 32% +600 bps QoQ/+28% YoY, 22% base vs. 14%; CMS OPPS 2,800 procs, 89 placements Regent/Surgical Care, 45 cases/mo/center.

Hospitals 78% util AI analytics -22% setup; ASCs +35% procs OrthoFlex 95% NPS same-day.

PrecisionNav 3.0 4K/kinematics +40% conversions; EHR HL7 Epic/Cerner -30% billing. U.S. 52%/38%, 320 reps top 1,200; Europe 41% +12% Germany/UK; APAC 25% China 45 Tier-1/Singapore +50%.

ASC margin expander 92% attach/$2.8k ASP vs. hospital 85%; $45 million CoE VR training/risk-share <2% readmits. Guide year-end 52-55%/37-40% ASCs, +$220 million disposables. 65% win vs. Mako/ROSA.

Finally, strategic priorities for next quarter. Post-strong Q4 12% rev $1.2 billion/18% structural heart vols/28% EBITDA, our Innovate-Expand-Optimize framework targets 15-20 bps share in $600 billion market/5.2% CAGR.

Pillars: Pipeline 40%—EvoGuard TAVR full U.S. ramp 5,000 procs/$250 million run-rate 92% success -25% leak $32k ASP NTAP; NeuroPulse DBS PMA AI/battery >Percept; robotics first-human vs. Mako $15 billion. R&D 14%.

Geographic 30%—APAC 28% Q4 to $180 million Japan EvoGuard/Terumo 40% 25k procs/China NRDL 35%; Europe 8-10% MDR CAPEX; U.S. 12% 50 GPOs Southeast ASC; int'l 42%.

Ops 20%—Resilient dual-source 85% platinum; Galway automation +200 bps 62% GM/ SAP 15% turns; Optum VBC CardioFlow -18% readmits $8 billion CRM.

Partnerships 10%—$300 million AI imaging/Philips JV India ortho $5 billion ASEAN; $1.2 billion FY M&A 5% EPS.

Q1 guide $1.3-1.32 billion 14-16% YoY/29-30% EBITDA/$0.85-0.90 EPS FCF >90%. FX/election/tariff hedged.

This roadmap outpaces peers in precision medtech.

I'll now turn the call over to John for financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Elena. As Elena outlined, we posted strong Q4 and full-year results. Full-year revenue hit $4.82 billion, up 18% reported/21% organic, with Q4 at $1.3 billion, +15% organic. Gross margin expanded 220 bps to 65.5%, driven by consumables mix, pricing, and manufacturing efficiencies from Costa Rica. Operating expenses rose 12% to $2.1 billion, R&D at 11.5%, SG&A disciplined. Adjusted operating margin hit 28.2%, up 180 bps. Adjusted EPS $1.72 for Q4, $6.45 full-year. Cash from ops $1.1 billion, FCF $850 million. Balance sheet solid, $2.5 billion cash, net debt/EBITDA 1.8x.

For FY2024, revenue $5.45-5.60 billion, 13-16% organic; adjusted EPS $6.85-7.05, assuming stable FX/reimbursement, $150 million synergies.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Michael Chen for our technology roadmap.

Dr. Michael Chen:
Thank you, John. We keep investing in cutting-edge tech. Development of InnoValve Ultra is on track and will revolutionize structural heart interventions with superior outcomes and efficiency.

Our pipeline builds on Q4 momentum: InnoClip Bio advancing trials, AccuStim neuromodulation EU approval imminent, InnoBot robotics precision scaling. R&D at 11-12% revenue sustains 28 programs, AI/digital integrations like CardioSense boosting remote monitoring. We've enhanced manufacturing with new labs, ensuring scalability for robotics base growth and bioresorbables. This positions us against peers in high-growth TAMs.

Next, Lisa with commercial insights.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our commercial team drove product adoption key to results. Focused on U.S. hospital/ASC expansion, where PrecisionNav/OrthoFlex adoption hit 48%/32%, plus EMEA/APAC tenders. Value-based contracts, GPO wins, and ASC CoE program lifted utilization and ASPs. Emerging markets like China/India via partnerships ramped structural heart/robotics. Sales force targeted high-volume sites, securing 127 hospital/89 ASC wins. Ahead, geographic push and launches like EvoGuard sustain mid-teens growth.

Now, back to Elena for Q&A.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions remain the same. Our first question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee - JPMorgan:
Thanks, and congrats on the strong year. On overall growth, how much of the 21% organic was procedure-driven versus share/pricing, and thoughts on durability into 2024?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, David. Procedures contributed about 12-14 points, aligning with industry recovery, while share gains added 5-6 points from launches like EvoFlow and VascuShield capturing 150-220 bps in key segments. Pricing +2-3% from premiums. Into 2024, backlog $3.4 billion and demographics support sustained double-digits, with new products ramping to 25% of growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen - Goldman Sachs:
Thanks. On margins, with consumables mix improving to 72%, can you quantify the impact and outlook for op margins amid R&D at 11.5%?

John Ramirez:
Hi Emily. Consumables shift drove ~150 bps gross margin expansion, 78% GM versus 62% capital. Total gross to 65.5%, ops to 28.2%. FY24 expect another 100-200 bps from mix/automation/synergies, targeting 29-30% EBITDA despite R&D steady 11-13%. Pricing discipline offsets inflation now at 2%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel - Morgan Stanley:
Good morning. Lisa, on commercial, adoption accelerated in ASCs to 32%—what's driving that and potential for further site-of-care shift?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Raj. ASC boom from CMS OPPS expansion to 2,800 procs, our minimally invasive portfolio enables it—OrthoFlex/PrecisionNav cut times, high NPS. Partnerships with Regent/Surgical Care added 89 sites, +35% volumes. Margins richer at 92% attach. Expect 37-40% year-end, more migration as payers push outpatient.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim - Barclays:
Thanks. Michael, pipeline looks robust—update on robotics timeline and competitive moat versus Intuitive/Stryker?

Dr. Michael Chen:
Sarah, InnoBot Precision first-human exceeded with sub-1mm accuracy at 30% lower cost/proc. EU funding de-risks IDE 2025. Moat from multi-specialty, AI integration/Siemens, and $50 million consortium. Targets $20 billion TAM +18% volumes, utilization ramping like da Vinci but broader ortho/neuro.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
